text:
Let $\mathrm{A}(x,y,z)$ be a point in $xy$-plane, which is equidistant from three points $(0,3,2),(2,0,3)$ and $(0,0,1)$.

Let $\mathrm{B}=(1,4,-1)$ and $\mathrm{C}=(2,0,-2)$. Then among the statements

(S1) : $△\mathrm{ABC}$ is an isosceles right angled triangle, and

(S2) : the area of $△\mathrm{ABC}$ is $\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}$,
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $A$ lies in the $xy$-plane, $A=(x,y,0)$.

Equating squared distances from $(2,0,3)$ and $(0,0,1)$:

$(x-2)^{2}+y^{2}+9=x^{2}+y^{2}+1\Rightarrow -4x+12=0\Rightarrow x=3$

Equating squared distances from $(0,3,2)$ and $(0,0,1)$:

$x^{2}+(y-3)^{2}+4=x^{2}+y^{2}+1\Rightarrow -6y+12=0\Rightarrow y=2$

So $A=(3,2,0)$. With $B=(1,4,-1)$ and $C=(2,0,-2)$:

$AB^{2}=4+4+1=9,AC^{2}=1+4+4=9,BC^{2}=1+16+1=18$

$AB=AC=3$ and $AB^{2}+AC^{2}=BC^{2}$, so $△ABC$ is isosceles and right-angled at $A$; (S1) is true.

$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot AC=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 3=\frac{9}{2}\neq \frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}$

so (S2) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

text: If $f(x)=\frac{2^{x}}{2^{x}+\sqrt{2}},\mathrm{x}\in \mathrm{ℝ}$, then $\sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}=1}^{81}f\left (\frac{\mathrm{k}}{82}\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(x)=\dfrac{2^{x}}{2^{x}+\sqrt{2}} \\ f(x)+f(1-x)=\dfrac{2^{x}}{2^{x}+\sqrt{2}}+\dfrac{2^{1-x}}{2^{1-x}+\sqrt{2}} \\ =\dfrac{2^{x}}{2^{x}+\sqrt{2}}+\dfrac{2}{2+\sqrt{2}2^{x}}=\dfrac{2^{x}+\sqrt{2}}{2^{x}+\sqrt{2}}=1 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Now,}\sum\limits _{\mathrm{k}=1}^{81}\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{\mathrm{k}}{82}\right )=\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{1}{82}\right )+\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{2}{82}\right )+\ldots \ldots +\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{81}{82}\right ) \\ =\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{1}{82}\right )+\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{2}{82}\right )+\ldots \ldots .+\mathrm{f}\left (1-\frac{2}{82}\right )+\mathrm{f}\left (1-\frac{1}{82}\right ) \\ =\left [\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{1}{82}\right )+\mathrm{f}\left (1-\frac{1}{82}\right )\right ]+\left [\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{2}{82}\right )+\mathrm{f}\left (1-\frac{2}{82}\right )\right ]+\ldots ..40\text{cases}+\mathrm{f}\left (\frac{41}{82}\right ) \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} =(1+1+\ldots 40\text{times})+\dfrac{2^{1/2}}{2^{1/2}+2^{1/2}} \\ 40+\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{81}{2} \end{array}$

text: The sum, of the squares of all the roots of the equation $x^{2}+|2x-3|-4=0$, is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the sum of the squares of all the roots of the equation $x^{2}+|2x-3|-4=0$:

Case I: $x\geq \frac{3}{2}$
For $x\geq \frac{3}{2}$, the expression $|2x-3|$ becomes $2x-3$. Thus, the equation becomes:

$x^{2}+2x-3-4=0$

Simplifying gives:

$x^{2}+2x-7=0$

Solving this quadratic equation, we find:

$x=2\sqrt{2}-1$

Case II: $x<\frac{3}{2}$
For $x<\frac{3}{2}$, the expression $|2x-3|$ becomes $-(2x-3)=-2x+3$. The equation therefore becomes:

$x^{2}+3-2x-4=0$

Simplifying gives:

$x^{2}-2x-1=0$

Solving this quadratic equation, we obtain:

$x=1-\sqrt{2}$

Sum of the Squares of the Roots
The sum of the squares of the roots is:

$(2\sqrt{2}-1)^{2}+(1-\sqrt{2})^{2}$

Calculating each term:

$(2\sqrt{2}-1)^{2}=(2\sqrt{2})^{2}-2\cdot 2\sqrt{2}\cdot 1+1^{2}=8-4\sqrt{2}+1=9-4\sqrt{2}$

$(1-\sqrt{2})^{2}=1^{2}-2\cdot 1\cdot \sqrt{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}=1-2\sqrt{2}+2=3-2\sqrt{2}$

Adding these results:

$(9-4\sqrt{2})+(3-2\sqrt{2})=12-6\sqrt{2}$

This simplifies to $6(2-\sqrt{2})$.

Thus, the sum of the squares of the roots is $6(2-\sqrt{2})$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

text: If $\int\limits _{-\frac{π}{2}}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{96x^{2}\cos ^{2}x}{(1+e^{x})}\mathrm{d}x=π\left (απ^{2}+β\right ),α,β\in \mathrm{ℤ}$, then $(α+β)^{2}$ equals
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $I=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}\dfrac{96x^{2}\cos ^{2}x}{1+e^{x}}dx$, replacing $x$ by $-x$ gives $I=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}\dfrac{96x^{2}\cos ^{2}xe^{x}}{1+e^{x}}dx$.

Adding the two forms, $2I=\int\limits _{-π/2}^{π/2}96x^{2}\cos ^{2}xdx=2\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}96x^{2}\cos ^{2}xdx$, since the integrand is even. So

$I=48\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}x^{2}(1+\cos 2x)dx=48\left [\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right ]_{0}^{π/2}+48\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}x^{2}\cos 2xdx$

The first part is $48\cdot \dfrac{π^{3}}{24}=2π^{3}$.

Integrating by parts twice, $\int x^{2}\cos 2xdx=\dfrac{x^{2}\sin 2x}{2}+\dfrac{x\cos 2x}{2}-\dfrac{\sin 2x}{4}$, so $\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}x^{2}\cos 2xdx=\dfrac{π}{2}\cdot \dfrac{\cos π}{2}-0=-\dfrac{π}{4}$.

Thus $I=2π^{3}-12π=π(2π^{2}-12)$, so $α=2$, $β=-12$ and $(α+β)^{2}=(-10)^{2}=100$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{r}}$ be the $\mathrm{r}^{\text{th}}$ term of an A.P. If for some $\mathrm{m},\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{1}{25},\mathrm{T}_{25}=\frac{1}{20}$, and $20\sum\limits _{\mathrm{r}=1}^{25}\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{r}}=13$, then $5\mathrm{m}\sum\limits _{\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{m}}^{2\mathrm{m}}\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{r}}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the first term be $a$ and the common difference $d$.

$20\sum\limits _{r=1}^{25}T_{r}=13\Rightarrow S_{25}=\dfrac{13}{20}$. Since $S_{25}=\dfrac{25}{2}(T_{1}+T_{25})$,

$T_{1}+T_{25}=\dfrac{13}{20}\times \dfrac{2}{25}=\dfrac{13}{250}\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{26}{500}-\dfrac{25}{500}=\dfrac{1}{500}$

$T_{25}=a+24d=\dfrac{1}{20}\Rightarrow 24d=\dfrac{25}{500}-\dfrac{1}{500}=\dfrac{24}{500}\Rightarrow d=\dfrac{1}{500}$, so $T_{r}=\dfrac{r}{500}$.

$T_{m}=\dfrac{m}{500}=\dfrac{1}{25}\Rightarrow m=20$.

The sum from $T_{20}$ to $T_{40}$ has 21 terms:

$\sum\limits _{r=20}^{40}T_{r}=\dfrac{21}{2}\left (\dfrac{20}{500}+\dfrac{40}{500}\right )=\dfrac{21}{2}\times \dfrac{60}{500}=\dfrac{63}{50}$

$5m\sum\limits _{r=m}^{2m}T_{r}=100\times \dfrac{63}{50}=126$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Let ABCD be a trapezium whose vertices lie on the parabola $\mathrm{y}^{2}=4\mathrm{x}$. Let the sides AD and BC of the trapezium be parallel to $y$-axis. If the diagonal AC is of length $\frac{25}{4}$ and it passes through the point $(1,0)$, then the area of $ABCD$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

For $y^{2}=4x$, $a=1$ and the focus is $S(1,0)$, so the diagonal $AC$ is a focal chord. With $A(t^{2},2t)$, the other end is $C\left (\dfrac{1}{t^{2}},-\dfrac{2}{t}\right )$, since the parameters of a focal chord satisfy $t_{1}t_{2}=-1$.

The focal distance of $(x,y)$ is $1+x$, so

$AC=AS+SC=(1+t^{2})+\left (1+\dfrac{1}{t^{2}}\right )=\left (t+\dfrac{1}{t}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{25}{4}$

Thus $t+\dfrac{1}{t}=\pm \dfrac{5}{2}$, so $t=\pm 2$ or $\pm \dfrac{1}{2}$; all four give the same trapezium up to reflection or relabelling. Taking $t=\dfrac{1}{2}$: $A\left (\dfrac{1}{4},1\right )$ and $C(4,-4)$.

$AD$ is parallel to the $y$-axis, so $D$ is the other point of the parabola with $x=\dfrac{1}{4}$: $D\left (\dfrac{1}{4},-1\right )$. Likewise $BC$ gives $B(4,4)$.

The parallel sides are $AD=2$ and $BC=8$, and the distance between them is $4-\dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{15}{4}$.

$\text{Area}=\dfrac{1}{2}(2+8)\times \dfrac{15}{4}=\dfrac{75}{4}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Let the equation of the circle, which touches $x$-axis at the point $(a,0),a>0$ and cuts off an intercept of length $b$ on $y$-axis be $x^{2}+y^{2}-αx+βy+γ=0$. If the circle lies below $x$-axis, then the ordered pair $\left (2a,b^{2}\right )$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

By Pythagoras $\mathrm{r}^{2}=\mathrm{a}^{2}+\frac{\mathrm{b}^{2}}{4}=\mathrm{P}^{2}$

$r=\sqrt{\frac{4a^{2}+b^{2}}{4}}$

Equation of circle is $(x-a)^{2}+(y-p)^{2}=r^{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} x^{2}+y^{2}-2ax-2py+a^{2}+p^{2}-r^{2}=0 \\ \text{comparison}x^{2}+y^{2}-αx+βy+γ=0 \\ -α=-2a,β=-2p,γ=a^{2} \\ \Rightarrow 2a=α,4a^{2}+b^{2}=4p^{2} \\ α^{2}+b^{2}=4p^{2} \\ α^{2}+b^{2}=β^{2} \end{array}$

So, $\left (2a,b^{2}\right )=\left (α,β^{2}-4γ\right )$

text: Let $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be a function defined by $f(x)=(2+3a)x^{2}+\left (\frac{a+2}{a-1}\right )x+b,a\neq 1$. If $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(\mathrm{y})+1-\frac{2}{7}x\mathrm{y}$, then the value of $28\sum\limits _{i=1}^{5}|f(i)|$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f(x)=(3a+2)x^{2}+\left (\dfrac{a+2}{a-1}\right )x+b \\ f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+1-\dfrac{2}{7}xy\text{.... (1)} \end{array}$

In (1) Put $x=y=0\Rightarrow f(0)=2f(0)+1\Rightarrow f(0)=-1$

So, $\mathrm{f}(0)=0+0+\mathrm{b}=-1\Rightarrow \mathrm{b}=-1$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{In (1) Put}y=-x\Rightarrow f(0)=f(x)+f(-x)+1+\dfrac{2}{7}x^{2} \\ -1=2(3a+2)x^{2}+2b+1+\dfrac{2}{7}x^{2} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} -1=\left (2(3a+2)+\dfrac{2}{7}\right )x^{2}+1-2 \\ \Rightarrow 6a+4+\dfrac{2}{7}=0 \\ a=-\dfrac{5}{7} \end{array}$

So $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=-\frac{1}{7}\mathrm{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{4}\mathrm{x}-1$

$\Rightarrow |\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})|=\frac{1}{28}\left |4\mathrm{x}^{2}+21\mathrm{x}+28\right |$

Now, $28\sum\limits _{i=1}^{5}|f(i)|=28(|f(1)|+|f(2)|+\ldots +|f(5)|)$

$28\cdot \frac{1}{28}\cdot 675=675$

text: Let $O$ be the origin, the point $A$ be $z_{1}=\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{2}i$, the point $B(z_{2})$ be such that $\sqrt{3}|z_{2}|=|z_{1}|$ and $\arg (z_{2})=\arg (z_{1})+\frac{π}{6}$. Then
options: ABO is an obtuse angled isosceles triangle
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$z_{1}=\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{2}i&\frac{|z_{2}|}{|z_{1}|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

given $\arg \left (\frac{z_{2}}{z_{1}}\right )=\frac{π}{6}$

$\begin{array}{l} z_{2}=\dfrac{|z_{2}|}{|z_{1}|}\cdot z_{1}\mathrm{e}^{i\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )} \\ z_{2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \dfrac{(\sqrt{3}+2\sqrt{2}i)(\sqrt{3}+i)}{2} \\ z_{2}=\dfrac{(3-2\sqrt{2})+i(2\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{3})}{2\sqrt{3}} \end{array}$

Now,

$z_{1}-z_{2}=\frac{(3+2\sqrt{2})+i(2\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{3})}{2\sqrt{3}}$

$|z_{1}-z_{2}|=|z_{2}|\Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{ABO}$ is isosceles with angles $\frac{π}{6},\frac{π}{6}&\frac{2π}{3}$

text:
Let M denote the set of all real matrices of order $3\times 3$ and let $\mathrm{S}=\{-3,-2,-1,1,2\}$. Let

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{S}_{1}=\left \{\mathrm{A}=[a_{\mathrm{ij}}]\in \mathrm{M}:\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\text{and}a_{\mathrm{ij}}\in \mathrm{S},\forall \mathrm{i},\mathrm{j}\right \}, \\ \mathrm{S}_{2}=\left \{\mathrm{A}=[a_{\mathrm{ij}}]\in \mathrm{M}:\mathrm{A}=-\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\text{and}a_{\mathrm{ij}}\in \mathrm{S},\forall \mathrm{i},\mathrm{j}\right \}, \\ \mathrm{S}_{3}=\{\mathrm{A}=[a_{\mathrm{ij}}]\in \mathrm{M}:a_{11}+a_{22}+a_{33}=0\text{and}a_{\mathrm{ij}}\in \mathrm{S},\forall \mathrm{i},\mathrm{j}\}. \end{array}$

If $n(S_{1}\cup S_{2}\cup S_{3})=125α$, then $α$ equals $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
All entries come from $S=\{-3,-2,-1,1,2\}$, which has 5 elements and does not contain 0.

For $S_{1}$ ($A=A^{T}$), the 3 diagonal entries and the 3 entries above the diagonal are free and fix the rest: $n(S_{1})=5^{3}\times 5^{3}=5^{6}$.

For $S_{2}$ ($A=-A^{T}$), every diagonal entry must be 0, which is not in $S$: $n(S_{2})=0$.

For $S_{3}$, the ordered diagonal triples $(a_{11},a_{22},a_{33})$ with sum 0 are the 6 orders of $(1,2,-3)$, the 3 orders of $(1,1,-2)$ and the 3 orders of $(-1,-1,2)$, that is 12 triples; the 6 off-diagonal entries are free: $n(S_{3})=12\times 5^{6}$.

A matrix in $S_{1}\cap S_{3}$ has one of the 12 diagonal triples and 3 free entries above the diagonal: $n(S_{1}\cap S_{3})=12\times 5^{3}$.

$n(S_{1}\cup S_{2}\cup S_{3})=5^{6}+12\times 5^{6}-12\times 5^{3}=5^{3}(13\times 125-12)=125\times 1613.$

Hence, the answer is 1613.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

solution.body: $\begin{array}{llll} \begin{array}{ll} α & =1+\sum\limits _{\mathrm{r}=1}^{6}(-1)^{\mathrm{r}-1}{}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{2\mathrm{r}-1}3^{\mathrm{r}-1} \\ α & =1+\sum\limits _{\mathrm{r}=1}^{6}{}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{2\mathrm{r}-1}\dfrac{(\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})^{2\mathrm{r}-1}}{\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i}}\mathrm{i}=\text{iota, let}\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i}=\mathrm{x} \\ α & =1+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i}}\left ({}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{1}\mathrm{x}+{}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{3}\mathrm{x}^{3}+\ldots .{}^{12}\mathrm{C}_{11}\mathrm{x}^{11}\right ) \\ =1+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i}}\left (\dfrac{(1+\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})^{12}-(1-\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i})^{12}}{2}\right ) \\ =1+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}\mathrm{i}}\left (\dfrac{\left (-2ω^{2}\right )^{12}-(2ω)^{12}}{2}\right )=1 \end{array} \\ \text{so distance of}(12,\sqrt{3})\text{from}x-\sqrt{3}y+1=0\text{is} \\ \dfrac{12-3+1}{2}=5 \end{array}$

text: Let $\mathrm{E}_{1}:\frac{x^{2}}{9}+\frac{y^{2}}{4}=1$ be an ellipse. Ellipses $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}$ 's are constructed such that their centres and eccentricities are same as that of $\mathrm{E}_{1}$, and the length of minor axis of $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{i}}$ is the length of major axis of $E_{i+1}(i\geq 1)$. If $A_{i}$ is the area of the ellipse $E_{i}$, then $\frac{5}{π}\left (\sum\limits _{i=1}^{\infty }A_{i}\right )$, is equal to $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $E_{1}$: $a_{1}=3$, $b_{1}=2$, so $e=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{4}{9}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ and $\dfrac{b_{1}}{a_{1}}=\sqrt{1-e^{2}}=\dfrac{2}{3}$.

Every $E_{i}$ has this eccentricity, so its semi-minor axis is $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of its semi-major axis: $b_{i}=\dfrac{2}{3}a_{i}$.


[IMG]

The semi-major axis of $E_{i+1}$ equals the semi-minor axis of $E_{i}$, so $a_{i+1}=b_{i}=\dfrac{2}{3}a_{i}$ and $b_{i+1}=\dfrac{2}{3}a_{i+1}=\dfrac{2}{3}b_{i}$.

Hence $A_{i+1}=πa_{i+1}b_{i+1}=\dfrac{4}{9}πa_{i}b_{i}=\dfrac{4}{9}A_{i}$: the areas $A_{1}=6π,A_{2}=\dfrac{8π}{3},A_{3}=\dfrac{32π}{27},\ldots$ form a GP with common ratio $\dfrac{4}{9}$.

$\sum\limits _{i=1}^{\infty }A_{i}=\frac{6π}{1-\frac{4}{9}}=\frac{54π}{5}\Rightarrow \frac{5}{π}\sum\limits _{i=1}^{\infty }A_{i}=54$

Hence, the answer is 54.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift

text: Let $⃗{a}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}},\vec{\mathrm{b}}=2\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{d}}=⃗{a}\times \vec{\mathrm{b}}$. If $\vec{\mathrm{c}}$ is a vector such that $⃗{a}\cdot \vec{\mathrm{c}}=|\vec{\mathrm{c}}|$, $|\vec{\mathrm{c}}-2⃗{a}|^{2}=8$ and the angle between $\vec{\mathrm{d}}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{c}}$ is $\frac{π}{4}$, then $|10-3\mathrm{b}\leftarrow \cdot \vec{\mathrm{c}}|+|\vec{\mathrm{d}}\times \vec{\mathrm{c}}|^{2}$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 28th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$⃗{d}=⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \end{array}\right |=-\hat{i}+\hat{j},|⃗{d}|=\sqrt{2}$

With $|⃗{a}|^{2}=3$ and $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=|⃗{c}|$:

$|⃗{c}-2⃗{a}|^{2}=|⃗{c}|^{2}-4⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}+4|⃗{a}|^{2}=|⃗{c}|^{2}-4|⃗{c}|+12=8\Rightarrow \left (|⃗{c}|-2\right )^{2}=0$

So $|⃗{c}|=2$ and $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c}=2$.

The angle between $⃗{d}$ and $⃗{c}$ is $\dfrac{π}{4}$:

$|⃗{d}\times ⃗{c}|=|⃗{d}||⃗{c}|\sin \dfrac{π}{4}=\sqrt{2}\times 2\times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=2\Rightarrow |⃗{d}\times ⃗{c}|^{2}=4$

By the vector triple product, with $x=⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c}$:

$⃗{d}\times ⃗{c}=(⃗{a}\times ⃗{b})\times ⃗{c}=(⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{c})⃗{b}-(⃗{b}\cdot ⃗{c})⃗{a}=2⃗{b}-x⃗{a}$

Using $|⃗{b}|^{2}=9$, $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}=5$ and $|⃗{a}|^{2}=3$:

$|2⃗{b}-x⃗{a}|^{2}=4(9)-4x(5)+3x^{2}=4\Rightarrow 3x^{2}-20x+32=0\Rightarrow (3x-8)(x-4)=0$

Both $x=\dfrac{8}{3}$ and $x=4$ occur for suitable $⃗{c}$, and both give the same value:

$x=\dfrac{8}{3}:|10-8|+4=6,x=4:|10-12|+4=6$

Hence, the answer is 6.
